bibl.title: A Monastic Origin of the Nag Hammadi Codices?
bibl.seg: Przemysław Piwowarczyk & Ewa Wipszycka, A Monastic Origin of the Nag Hammadi Codices?
bibl.note: À propos de: Hugo Lundhaug & Lance Jenott, The Monastic Origins of the Nag Hammadi Codices = Studien und Texte zu Antike und Christentum. 97 (Tübingen, 2015). - Introduction. - 1. The dossier of papyri from the covers of the Nag Hammadi codices. - 2. Gnostics and monks. - 3. Monastic mentalities and Nag Hammadi codices. - 4. Apocryphal Books in Egyptian monasteries: 4.1. Pseudo-Euodius and John of Parallos; - 4.2. Apocrypha in the catalogues of monastic libraries preserved on papyri; - 4.3. Apocrypha in book collections of the Egyptian monasteries; - 4.4. Apocrypha in the Pachomian libraries; - 4.5. Shenoute's discourse I Am Amazed and Dioscorus' letter to Shenoute; - 4.6. The issue of ownership of the Codex Berolinensis; - 4.7. Readers of apocrypha in late antique Egypt. - 5. Scribal notes in the Nag Hammadi codices. - 6. Nag Hammadi codices and the Dishna Papers. - Conclusion.
